You're designing a part for someone to 3D print at home. They'll print it on their own printer, use only the hardware listed below, and put it together by following your manual.

## Their setup
- Printer: Bambu Lab X1C (with AMS), build volume 256 x 256 x 256 mm
- Nozzle: 0.4 mm
- Layer height: 0.2 mm
- Filament: PLA (high-speed PLA, black)
- Longest bridge seen to print cleanly on this setup: 50 mm

## Hardware they can use
Refer to an item by its catalog reference: "ISO 4762 M5x30" (socket head screw, size x length, from the lengths listed), "ISO 4032 M5" (hex nut), "ISO 10511 M5" (nylon-insert lock nut), "ISO 7089 M5" (washer), "ASME B18.2.2 1/4-20" (1/4"-20 nut), "insert M3x4x5" (heat-set insert), "salvaged:webcam-mount-bolt".

## Their own parts
The person has these too, for this design only. Refer to each by its reference, such as "own:led-disk". What isn't listed hasn't been measured: ask them.

```yaml
- ref: own:led-disk
  kind: board
  description: 'Adafruit DotStar RGB LED Disk, product 2477 (Soya LED SY-C255-102): 255 APA102C LEDs on a round, rigid white circuit board, with its input wires on a 4-pin connector'
  frame: origin at the centre of the board's back face (the side without LEDs); +z out through the LED side; +y towards where its input wires leave
- ref: own:perfboard
  kind: board
  description: their perfboard, with an ESP32-S3 DevKitC-1 (N16R8) plugged into female headers, screw terminals and a capacitor soldered on, and four wires running to the disk's input; it has four holes, one in each corner
  frame: origin at the centre of the board's top face (the side the ESP32 is on); +z up from that face; +y along the board's long side
- ref: own:esp32
  kind: board
  description: the ESP32 on the perfboard; a USB-C wall charger plugs straight into its own USB-C port to power the light
  frame: origin at the centre of the mouth of the ESP32's USB-C port; +x straight out of the port, the way a plug's cable leaves it; +z up from the ESP32's top face; y along the mouth's long side
- ref: own:m2x6-self-tapping
  kind: screw
  description: M2 x 6 self-tapping screws
  d: 2
  length: 6
```

## How to work
You have these tools:
- measure(item, what): ask the person to measure one of their own things, such as their desk or their phone. They answer with what they measured, or say they can't measure it.
- submit_design(...): hand in the finished design. This ends the conversation.
- report_limitation(wanted, blocked_by, why): say you wanted to use something (a technique, a tool, a part or material, a way of handing in the design) but couldn't because of what's available here. It doesn't change anything, but it's noted.
You have at most 8 turns. Hand in a design before they run out.

## The design you hand in
submit_design's schema describes every field. The rules that matter:
- Every dimension that comes from hardware or the real world is a named param, with its source: measured (the person measured it for you), datasheet, catalog, asked (the person told you), guessed, unknown, or design (your own choice).
- Each part's `code` is Python that defines build(p) and returns a CadQuery Workplane or Shape. `cq` is already imported, and p.<name> is each param's value. Dimensions that come from hardware or the real world must come from params.
- Model each part in the orientation it's printed in, with z = 0 on the bed.
- The manual is the steps the person follows, naming the parts and hardware each step uses.
- Say where each final part and each of their own parts with a frame goes in the finished piece, and where each screw goes, in `assembly`.

I'm making a round light to hang on my wall: an Adafruit DotStar LED disc, the 255-LED one. I'll 3D print the front and sides in transparent PLA, so they look frosted and you can't make out the diodes, and the box behind the disc in matte white. The front and sides come later: for now I only need that box, with the disc screwed onto it. Inside it is an ESP32 on a perfboard, with four wires from the perfboard to the disc. The disc screws onto the front of the box with M3 screws, through two small holes near its centre. The holes aren't on its datasheet. The box hangs flat against the wall on two screws, and I power it with a USB-C charger plugged straight into the ESP32, so I need to reach its port from outside once it's all closed up.
I'll start with the measurements the box depends on.

I'm working out how the wires get from the perfboard to the disc, which means a passage through the lid, and since the connector's position is unknown I'm weighing a slot or notch near the top edge. The disc would sit on raised bosses around the insert holes so the wires have room underneath.

I'm considering a wire channel groove in the lid's front face running from the wire hole out to the top edge, and I'm weighing the lid thickness against the groove depth to fit the wires.

I'm weighing a raised ring or pads on the lid to leave a gap behind the disc for the wires and connector, though the connector may sit outside the box radius anyway. I'm also sketching a round box about 140mm across with the perfboard laid long-axis along x.

I'm placing the perfboard long-axis along y with the port edge facing down, so the cable hangs out the bottom. For a round box about 140mm across, the inner wall curves in toward the port, so the bottom edge has to clear that curve at the sides as well as the centre.

I'm settling on a rounded rectangle for the box rather than a circle, since the port edge would otherwise curve away from the perfboard. I'm sizing the outer shell around 90 by 120mm with a 3mm wall, leaving enough room inside for the wire bosses and lid screws.

I'm placing the bosses for the disc inserts on the lid's inner side and checking that they clear the ESP32, which sits about 2mm below the lid's inner face.

I'm sizing the keyhole for the wall-hanging screws: a 10 mm entry hole with a 4.8 mm slot, since #8 screws have a 4.2 mm shank and 9 mm heads. The back needs a raised pocket around each slot so the head sits behind the lip with about 3 mm of room.

I'm placing the keyhole blocks at about x=±30, y=+35, with the cavity above the 3mm back plate sized to hold the screw head, and checking that the blocks stay clear of the inner wall.

I'm placing the keyhole slots so the screw heads drop through the larger entry holes and then slide up into the narrower slots. That puts the entry near the bottom of each block and the rest point higher up, and I'm shifting the blocks up a little so they clear the perfboard's top edge.

I'm checking whether the boss at the lid corner clashes with the keyhole block, and it does overlap slightly in both x and y. So I'm shifting the keyhole block inward to clear it.

I'm placing the perfboard standoffs at about 23mm either side of centre, with 5mm-tall posts and M2 pilot holes, and checking that the nearest ones stay clear of the keyhole blocks.

I'm sizing the lid screws now: an M3x6 counterbored into a 5mm lid, so the head sits below the disc face and the screw reaches into a 6mm-deep insert hole.

I'm sizing the disc inserts at x=±16.75, which means a boss under the lid for the screws. Checking the ESP32's top at about 25.6mm, a 1mm boss keeps it clear of the board, but the bosses may still crowd the chip's centred footprint, so I'll look at the spacing again.
